scope: Software validation of a new Part 1 experiment; not proof of an improved leaderboard result or a completed pretrained CUDA run.
changes: One answering response selects short model source readings before composing an answer and choosing a status.
Earlier assistant claims are omitted from the evidence prompt; original user turns and source documents remain available.
Current explicit assumptions join the chronologically ordered, conversation-only assumptions.
Tables use one row-addressed representation with original headers, values, signs and parentheses.
Exact numbered-object citation metadata supplies matching figure references; unrelated references remain validation errors.
Checkpoint identity binds the new policy and option, preventing old measured answers from being relabeled as new results.
New CSV is published as submission_part1_v7.csv before the separate evaluation.

local_checks.fixture_integration: Both old and new policies exercised actual prediction, strict repair, dense/hybrid evaluation, citation-judge validation, official CSV validation, publication and ZIP export with fictional models/data. No fixture answers are lab results.
local_checks.tiny_model_scope: Random-weight Qwen image forwards check nested structured-decoding interfaces, not answer quality.

limitations: No local CUDA GPU was available. A full new Kaggle run is required to measure factual accuracy, score, memory use and wall time.
Model observations are not independently certified facts; only source membership and metadata consistency are validated by this policy.
The new answer format can change quality and runtime in either direction. No 0.8 score, error-free GPU execution or 90-minute completion is guaranteed.
Required human ratings, team review, final report and external submission remain separate from automated computation.
